_provenance.note: Not reachable from this sandbox at authoring time (no live GitLab mirror — same posture as every other gitlab-* fixture; CP-A3b live smoke deferred to the self-hosted phase). Hand-authored from the documented GitLab REST API v4 response shapes: notes (https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/api/notes.html — id, body, author.username, created_at, system) and merge-request approvals (https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/api/merge_request_approvals.html — approved_by[].user.username).
_provenance.shape_note: This is the only fixture in the suite whose `data` is an OBJECT keyed by endpoint rather than one response payload, because gitlab.mjs#prReviews is the only verb that reads TWO endpoints (issue #317): notes carry the verdict thread, approvals carry the L6 approver roster. The contract suite's gitlab glue dispatches on the request URL to serve the matching half.
_provenance.content_note: The notes list deliberately mixes all three classes the normalizer must tell apart: a GitLab SYSTEM note (dropped — activity record, never reviewer speech), a plain human comment (kept, no verdict block), and a reviewer verdict note carrying a real brain-review/1 fenced block (kept, and the one the contract suite feeds through parseVerdict). `created_at` is ascending, matching the sort=asc the verb requests. The approver in `approved_by` is a DIFFERENT identity from every note author, so a test asserting notes never normalize to state:'APPROVED' cannot pass by coincidence.
